name: Sage Green
lede: Sage Green is the soft grey-green of the leaves of the sage plant.

sections.title: The leaf of a herb
sections.body:
Paterson defines sage-green as the greyish or yellowish green of the leaves of the sage plant [1]. It appears in his index of greens, with [[sap-green]] close by [2][3]. The books give no date for the name or story beyond that definition [1].

The swatch is a muted green. Paterson lists sage-green and [[sage-grey]] as separate, consecutive entries [1][2]; see also [[sage]] and [[olive-green]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 278 hold this color at 5% of the canvas or more, as photographed [4]. The earliest strong sample is a portrait of Prince Murad Baksh from 1655 [4]. Printed use of *sage green* peaked in 1951 and stayed fairly high through the century [5]. The match counts any painting with this color covering at least a twentieth of the canvas, so it shows where the color appears in photographs of paintings, not that the painters ever called it by this name.
